title: IaaS, PaaS, SaaS
text: Think of M-Pesa. Using the M-Pesa app is SaaS: Safaricom runs everything and you just use it. Renting an empty shop stall and bringing your own fridge and staff is IaaS: the landlord gives the space, you run the rest. PaaS sits in the middle, like a stall that already has shelves and electricity, and you only bring your goods.

title: Shared responsibility
text: A landlord secures the building and the gate, but you lock your own shop door. In the cloud, Microsoft secures the datacenters; you always stay responsible for your data, accounts and access. How much else you manage depends on IaaS, PaaS or SaaS.

title: CapEx vs OpEx
text: Buying a router and generator outright is CapEx: a big upfront cost. Buying mobile data bundles is OpEx: you pay as you use, and top up when needed. Cloud consumption pricing works like data bundles.

title: Elasticity and scalability
text: A market trader hires extra helpers on market day and sends them home afterwards. Elasticity does that automatically for your app: more capacity during a rush, less when it’s quiet, so you only pay for what you need.

title: Regions and Availability Zones
text: A bakery with kitchens in separate parts of town can keep selling if one loses power. A region is a city-sized area; Availability Zones are separate datacenters inside it, each with its own power and cooling.

title: Blob Storage
text: A big storeroom where you keep boxes of different shapes: photos, videos, PDFs. Blob Storage holds unstructured files like these, while a database is more like an organised ledger book.

title: Microsoft Entra ID
text: Your M-Pesa PIN plus the SMS confirmation is a good picture of multifactor authentication: two different proofs it’s really you. Entra ID is the cloud identity service that checks who people are and what they may access.

title: Azure Policy
text: A town council by-law says, for example, where stalls may be set up. Azure Policy is the by-law book for your cloud: it can block or flag resources that break your organisation’s rules.

title: Resource locks
text: A padlock on the cash box: even people with the key to the shop can’t accidentally empty it. A resource lock stops accidental deletion or change, even by users who have permission.

title: Serverless / Azure Functions
text: Like paying a motorbike courier per delivery instead of owning a delivery van. Serverless runs your code only when something triggers it, and you don’t manage the server.

title: Public, private, hybrid
text: A public cloud is like using M-Pesa agents everyone shares. A private cloud is a till kept only in your own shop. Hybrid is both: sensitive records stay in your own till, while busy-season sales go through the shared agents.

title: Regions and scopes
text: Think of a supermarket chain: each branch is a region, and two sister branches are a region pair that take turns closing for maintenance. Scopes nest like the company, then a regional office, then a department: management group, subscription, resource group.

title: Networking
text: A virtual network is your private compound. Peering is a gate between two compounds, a VPN is a trusted tunnel through the public road, and ExpressRoute is your own private road. A private endpoint is a side door only your staff can use.

title: Storage tiers and copies
text: Hot is goods on the shop counter, cool is the back shelf, archive is the locked warehouse that takes hours to open. Redundancy is keeping copies: LRS in one room, ZRS in several buildings, GRS in another town.

title: Security basics
text: Zero Trust is a guard who checks every ID, every time, even for regulars. Defense in depth is the gate, the door, the safe and the CCTV together. RBAC gives the cashier a till key but not the safe key.

title: Cost, tools and monitoring
text: Tags are labels on your stock boxes so you know which department spent what. Reservations are like prepaying a year of airtime for a discount. Azure Advisor is a friendly consultant, Service Health tells you about outages, and ARM templates are your written recipe so every branch opens identically.
